SUPERVISOR — MIRROR SYMMETRY BREAK, USER report with the perfect test case. Marker: MIRRORSYM-0606 (resolve req by match).

USER, verbatim: "does this even make sense? why is the two sides of the mesh different if its a mirror image drawing?" Screenshots: 34.png (the mesh: LEFT side smooth rounded bumps, RIGHT side sharp angular shards — visibly different) and 35.png (the canvas: a cleanly mirror-symmetric drawing around the center meridian).

A symmetric grid MUST produce a symmetric mesh. Diagnose with their exact drawing as the repro, numerically: sample mirrored cell pairs (u, 1-u) — equal grid values? Then mirrored VERTEX displacements on the mesh — equal? Find where symmetry dies:
(a) the grid→mesh mapping (seam topology: does u=0/1 wrap meet a different vertex density than the u=0.5 mirror line?),
(b) the BASE mesh already asymmetric from prior grab-sculpts (depth compounds on existing geometry — test: reset part, redraw the symmetric shape, still asymmetric?),
(c) the apply path (mirror stamp sign/scale/rounding differing per side),
(d) display vs data (smooth shading hiding that the data IS symmetric — check before assuming).
Post the numbers, then fix at the true layer. P4 pin: symmetric grid in → mirrored vertex pairs equal within epsilon. READY FOR USER TEST with their own drawing.
